name: Barbegal mill complex
summary: Barbegal near Arles: sixteen Roman watermills in two stepped rows of eight, fed by an aqueduct, one of the largest machine complexes of the ancient world.
description: Two rows of eight watermills supplied by the redirected southern aqueduct branch.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

impact.note: One site scaling up existing watermilling for one city, later abandoned with no known descendants; implies tier 3, below reviewed tier 2.

date.label: First half of the second century CE
date.basis: The excavation report dates the building to the first half of the second century. The 2018 site account estimates the diversion around 120–130 CE, and the 2024 synthesis gives the diversion at century resolution.

events.statement: The excavators date construction of the Barbegal mill complex to the first half of the second century CE. Its two rows of eight watermills were supplied by the redirected southern aqueduct branch.
events.caveats: The exact construction and commissioning dates remain uncertain. Wooden wheels are lost. Exact housing, output and customer reconstructions are outside this node.

evidence.locator: p. 389, introduction; p. 436, Conclusion, first paragraph
evidence.supports: The excavators revise construction of the complex from the third century to the first half of the second century.

evidence.locator: Results, The Barbegal site, paragraph 1; Fig. 1
evidence.supports: Configuration, supply relationship and a narrower estimate of the diversion around 120–130 CE.
Detached branch and new parallel aqueduct bridge feeding the mill complex.

date.label: by 300 CE
date.basis: Carbonate records years of operations; the source inherits an early-third-century archaeological abandonment date. 300 is a conservative upper bound, not a measured commissioning year.

events.statement: The mill complex operated for years after the aqueduct was diverted and before its early-third-century abandonment.
events.population: Operators of the Barbegal mill complex near Arelate
events.caveats: The early-third-century dating is an inherited archaeological interpretation, not a precise date measured from the carbonate; the first operational day and customers are unknown.

evidence.locator: Results, The Barbegal site; Results and Discussion, carbonate deposits and end of operation
evidence.supports: Describes the diverted aqueduct, mill-run carbonate formed over several decades, and abandonment in the early third century.

earliest_record.rationale: The excavation report provides an approximate construction range for the complex. The first day of operation and the exact timing of the diversion remain uncertain.

links.statement: A branch previously supplying Arelate was redirected to supply the Barbegal mills.
links.alternatives: Other water sources or new conduits were possible; no counterfactual cost comparison.
links.caveats: Historical relationship supported; Barbegal’s later diffusion influence is unknown.
links.timing: The 2018 site account places city-supply use before diversion to the mills around 120–130 CE.

evidence.supports: Explicit previous city use and subsequent diversion.
Explicit detachment and connection by a new parallel bridge.

unresolved.about: Dates of construction and first operation
unresolved.note: Compare the masonry, carbonate and associated artefact evidence for the mill building and diversion at the convergence basin. The excavators interpret the eastern outlet’s pottery deposit as later than construction.

evidence.locator: p. 436, Conclusion, paragraph on ceramics at the eastern outlet
evidence.supports: The excavators tentatively assign the pottery deposit to activity after construction, possibly associated with a modification of the outlet.
